name: Transient splice: attack of one source + body of another (wave-sequence / concatenative hybrid)
goal: Build a hybrid voice by concatenating the short attack/transient (~first 30–100 ms) of one sample or wave with the sustained body of another: either in one layer with a step sequence (very short first step, long crossfaded second step, loop start/end on the body step only) or across two layers (layer A gated transient with a short amp envelope, layer B looping body) so each part gets its own filter/FX while still fusing perceptually.

source.title: Wave Sequencing Synthesis: What Is It and How To Do It (Korg Wavestate Tutorial)

prerequisites: Synth or sampler with step/wave-sequence lanes (per-step sample, duration, crossfade, loop start/end) OR two layers each with its own amp envelope; library of original/free attack and sustain sources

inputs.name: attack_source
inputs.description: Source whose first 30–100 ms gives the recognisable transient (e.g. a piano-like or pluck strike)

inputs.name: body_source
inputs.description: Sustaining source for the body/decay (e.g. reed/flute-like or synth wave)

outputs.name: hybrid_voice
outputs.description: Voice whose onset reads as source A and whose sustain is source B, fused into one new sound

constraints: Ground every step in the source YouTube-provided Show-transcript text; do not invent UI paths or numeric settings not stated there.
Original synthesis / signal-flow only — map brand UI to portable osc/filter/env/LFO/FX modules for Traveler-inspired or Web Audio hybrid; never rip presets, wavetables, or samples.
Not affiliated with the plugin/hardware vendors named in the source video; recreate with comparable modules.
Portable alias: 'wave sequencing' = concatenative synthesis = per-step sample lane + timing lane + loop points.
Use original/free samples; do not copy factory multisample names.
Delta vs osc-as-granular-pitch-step-delay and wavetable-crossfade-morph-modulate-pad: this splices attack vs body of different sources, not pitch steps or WT position morphs.

steps.action: Think of each sound as two parts: attack/transient (first ~30–50 ms, noisy and carrying most of the identity) and body/decay (sustained, less noisy). The goal is to graft A's attack onto B's body.
steps.expect: Plan names which source supplies attack vs body

steps.action: Single-layer method: in the sample/step lane put the attack source on step 1 and the body source on step 2.
Timing lane: make step 1 very short (~0.1 s, try down to ~50 ms with smaller crossfade) and step 2 long with a generous crossfade so the switch is inaudible.
steps.expect: Only A's transient is heard before B's sustain

steps.action: Set loop start AND loop end on step 2 so the sequence plays step 1 once and then loops only the body; if loop start stays on step 1 the transient retriggers and clicks.
steps.expect: No repeating transient or click while the note is held

steps.action: Probe the limit: shorten step 1 and its crossfade until the attack identity becomes imperceptible, then back off. Swap attack sources (piano-like, pluck, guitar-like) over the same body to audition hybrids.
steps.expect: Attack still recognisable at the chosen length

steps.action: Two-layer method: layer A plays only the attack source with timing set to Gate (single step, no continuation) and an amp envelope with near-zero sustain and very short decay; layer B loops only the body source with its own amp envelope.
steps.expect: A is a short click/strike, B is the sustained tone

steps.action: Balance levels/envelopes so A is audible over B, then process them separately (filter, LFOs, compression, FX per layer) and add shared reverb/delay to glue them.
steps.expect: Separate timbral control of attack and body; still fuses as one note

verification: Muting the attack layer/step leaves only the body sound; muting the body leaves only a short transient
Holding a note produces no repeated transient or loop click
Listeners identify the onset as source A even though the sustain is source B
